- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 10–20% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 2.0), model frequently overcorrects with exaggerated downward moves; cap downward forecasts at 1.5–1.8 unless sentiment confirms continuation.  
- If history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days above 2.0), model often fails to revert; forecast should be pulled toward recent 7-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply a 5–15% downward bias to first 7 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.33), model exhibits erratic behavior; smooth forecasts using 3-day moving average of sentiment-weighted history.
